title: O Thou, Who Hast Thy Servants Taught
description: O Thou, Who Hast Thy Servants Taught in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Alford wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 482, “Sincere Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, who hast Thy ser-vants taught That not by words a-lone, But by the fruits of ho-li-ness, The life of God is shown;

lines: O Thou, who hast Thy servants taught
But by the fruits of holiness,
The life of God is shown;
While in Thy house of prayer we meet,
And call Thee God and Lord,
Give us a heart to follow Thee,
When we our voices lift in praise,
Give Thou us grace to bring
And in the dangerous path of life
That with our lips and in our lives

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Alford died in 1871.
credits: Words by Henry Alford (1810–1871), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
